messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE: high error rate - streaming decode OOMs observed in runtime-gpu-pool-us-west-2. Pager: @sara is on-call.

sara: seeing a spike in CUDA OOMs on decode nodes, lots of container restarts. Are we dropping streaming responses?

ben: yes, customers hitting streaming endpoints see partial streams then disconnects. Logs show repeated `std::bad_alloc` / cudaMalloc failures during decode.

raj: can you paste the snippet of the OOM stack? also list affected instance ids.

sara: copy/paste from node g-rd-23: ```
E CudaAllocator: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (2)
  at inference/decode_loop.cpp:342
  stack: decode_step -> kv_cache_alloc -> cudaMalloc
container_restart: crashloop backoff after SIGABRT
```

kai: rack g-rd-23 / g-rd-24 both noisy. Memory high prior to crash; looks like runaway generation requests with huge `max_tokens` and no rate limiting.

oncall-bot: Handoff requested: @sara -> @ben in 10m. Escalation threshold reached (customer impact).

ben: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle `streaming.max_tokens` via ingress gateway to 1024 for problematic model route, 2) enable token_limit middleware to kill runaway requests pre-decode, 3) route new traffic to fallback smaller model variant, 4) scale up ephemeral swap/pager capacity if needed. I'll start 1 and 3.

sara: doing 1 now - ingress config patch: ```yaml
- match: route:/v1/stream/gen
  actions:
    set_header:
      x-max-tokens: "1024"
```
apply: `kubectl apply -f ingress-patch.yaml --context=prod-us-west-2`

deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/ingress-patch by ben. CI checks passed.

ben: live: ingress now sets x-max-tokens=1024 for streaming route. Observability: throttles should drop long requests at gateway.

customer-support: getting multiple reports from a large customer about truncated transcripts and reconnects, they've opened a support ticket.

raj: enabling token_limit middleware (hotpatch) on runtime pool: `kubectl -n runtime patch deployment decode-runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"TOKEN_MAX","value":"1024"}]}]}}}}'`

kai: token_limit env applied on g-rd-23/g-rd-24, rolling restart started. Will watch for OOMs.

ben: also taking canary traffic and shifting 30% to `redwood/decoder-small:v2` via smart-routing to reduce memory footprint.

sara: post-change: OOMs dropped by ~80% on g-rd-23, container restarts reduced. Still seeing occasional decode spikes from queued requests.

oncall-bot: customer-impact update requested — please post ETA and customers affected.

customer-support: ticket #C-18342 impacted by partial stream disconnects starting 17:05 UTC; business-critical but no data loss reported. They've been notified of mitigation steps.

ben: root cause hypothesis: unbounded `max_tokens` and insufficient request-level guarding allowed some clients to request very long generations that forced large KV allocations during decode, blowing GPU memory and causing CUDA OOMs -> container crashes -> request drops.

raj: evidence: correlation between high `tokens_requested` field in request logs and subsequent cudaMalloc failures. Also one client was replaying a prompt loop.

sara: next steps (short): 1) keep ingress token cap and token_limit middleware, 2) add per-connection streaming timeout (60s), 3) temporary ramp of fallback routing to 50% until stability.

kai: longer term: add low-cost pre-parse to reject suspicious `max_tokens` > 4096, add kernel-friendly quantized variant routing for long-context, and automated `max_tokens` bot alerts.

ben: I'm preparing a customer-facing blurb with support that apologizes and explains mitigations + ETA for perf. Draft: "We've applied throttles and routed you to a stable model variant; you may see shorter generations while we stabilize. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

sara: monitoring: CPU/GPU memory and decode OOMs are stable for 12m. I'll keep the channel open for 30m then hand back to oncall rotation.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete: @ben -> @sara. Secondary: @raj. Incident status: mitigation in place, monitoring.

raj: capturing logs and making a runbook entry for similar future incidents. I'll open a postmortem ticket and include reproduction steps.

sara: thanks all — if anyone sees another crash ping here immediately. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout complete: smart-routing adjustments active.

ben: closing loop with customer support now.

customer-support: informed customer, they've acknowledged and will monitor.

sara: marking this thread resolved for active remediation; will keep an incident follow-up for analysis and concrete remediation tasks.
